label: prf:isotope-knot-equivalence
title: Proof of isotope knot equivalence
html:
Proof. Proof of isotope knot equivalence

Proof.

  • Reflexivity: K \sim K by definition since w_{q^Z}^{(1)} = w_{q^Z}^{(2)} = w_{q^Z} for K_1 = K_2.

  • Symmetry: K_1 \sim K_2 iff w_{q^Z}^{(1)} = w_{q^Z}^{(2)}, which is symmetric in K_1, K_2.

  • Transitivity: If w_{q^Z}^{(1)} = w_{q^Z}^{(2)} and w_{q^Z}^{(2)} = w_{q^Z}^{(3)}, then w_{q^Z}^{(1)} = w_{q^Z}^{(3)} by transitivity of equality in S_{n(K)}.

The equivalence classes at fixed Z are parameterized by the neutron-quark block w_{\bar q^N} and the inter-nucleon connector w_{\mathrm{inter}}. This gives the standard isotope chart for element Z (for example, Z = 6: {}^{12}\mathrm{C}, {}^{13}\mathrm{C}, {}^{14}\mathrm{C}, \ldots). \square

Quotient structure. The quotient \{\text{atom-knots}\}/{\sim} at fixed Z is the element class for Z. This recovers the chemical element concept categorically: an element is an isotope class.
